candidate_tasks.primary_question: Does a replay of the durable activation sequence under a queue-order selection policy reach the same signal-class coverage as frontier-first selection?
candidate_tasks.bottleneck: The strict counterfactual for the selector's efficiency advantage is unavailable, so the coverage and non-duplication benefit is observed but its magnitude versus queue-order selection is unquantified.
candidate_tasks.objective: Replay the durable activation history under both a queue-order policy and the frontier-first policy to compare which signal-class cells each would have selected by this point.
candidate_tasks.scope: Use only the durable activation records, LEARNING_STATE, STATE, and the campaign queue; no new experiments and no controller changes.
candidate_tasks.out_of_scope: Do not modify the controller, add a numerical reward score, or run new research backtests.
candidate_tasks.deliverable: A bounded comparison of coverage and duplication under the two selection policies, with a RETAIN/REJECT/UNVERIFIED process decision.
candidate_tasks.success_criterion: The comparison classifies whether frontier-first strictly dominates, ties, or underperforms queue-order selection on observable coverage, or records the comparison as unverified.
candidate_tasks.stop_condition: Stop when the durable sequence has been replayed under both policies and the coverage comparison is complete or clearly unverifiable.
candidate_tasks.verification_requirement: Controller-side schema validation plus independent inspection of the cited durable activation records.
candidate_tasks.evidence_basis: The prior opportunistic period (7 MA-family cells; activation 37260572520 UNVERIFIED process delta) and the frontier-first period (distinct signal-class cells) are both durable, so a replay would isolate the selection-policy effect.
